target_customer: Financial advisors and accredited investors seeking alternative investments such as hedge funds
problem: Alternative investments required manual paperwork and had poor reporting; Sliced digitized subscription signing and reporting.
business_model: Platform fees on alternative investment allocations by advisors and accredited investors

founders.name: Mike Furlong
founders.background_notes: Financial Samurai describes both founders as former Wall Street traders; specific employers not named.

founders.name: Akhil Lodha
founders.background_notes: Described with Furlong as a former Wall Street trader.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed electronic subscription document signing and integrations with custodians and reporting platforms, standard fintech integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with custodians create lock-in, but relationships with fund managers were the real asset and the product was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying was found; Sliced merged with StratiFi in early 2016.

market_need_then: Advisors faced paper-heavy alternative investment processes. Financial Samurai coverage and the funding round indicate investor interest, but no usage numbers were found.

rebrands.why: Merged into StratiFi, per Dealroom and CB Insights; the Financial Samurai post also mentions a merger with LOGe Solutions to form StratiFi.

brand_strength.rationale: Press about the company was launch and funding coverage only; no brand pages or community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Sliced raised a 2 million seed in November 2014 from Khosla Ventures and others, then merged into StratiFi in January 2016 per Dealroom and CB Insights. Financial Samurai says Sliced shut down and describes a 2016 merger creating StratiFi. No later round or stated cause was found, so the failure cause is not public beyond the absence of a follow-on round, which is an inference.
notes: YC lists status Acquired; sources describe a merger into StratiFi. Cross-check for the seed: FinSMEs and Hedgeweek both report 2M; investor list from search summaries since I did not open them. A TriplePoint investor was named inconsistently so it is omitted. No company website listed, so no site was fetched. The 'could_not_raise_next_round' factor is a weak inference, as no source states the cause. No dated competitor found: iCapital's platform launched in 2014 per InvestmentNews but I did not open it.
